formative_worksheets.title: Numerals 0-10 Check-In
formative_worksheets.when_to_use: After Lesson 3, before Lesson 4. A 10-minute mid-unit check that confirms A6.11 (number bonds to 5) and A6.12 (situations to 10) have landed before Day 4 introduces equal sharing.
formative_worksheets.purpose: Standalone formative assessment distinct from lesson worksheets. Lets the teacher quickly see which children can fluently recall partners of 5 and choose the right operation for a story to 10.
formative_worksheets.student_learning_goal: I can recall my partners of 5 and pick the right operation for a story to 10.

header.student_learning_goal_banner: I can recall my partners of 5 and pick the right operation for a story to 10.
header.character_watermark: Penny the Lead Counter in the top-right corner with a small magnifying glass — the 'check-in' Penny. Small (~1.5in tall).

prompts.prompt: Penny is hiding some cubes! She has 5 cubes total. Look at how many are showing and write how many are hidden.
prompts.visual_layout: Three Partner Hunt scenes side-by-side. Each scene shows a row of 5 cubes with Penny's hand drawn covering some. Scene A: 2 cubes visible (3 hidden). Scene B: 4 cubes visible (1 hidden). Scene C: 0 cubes visible (5 hidden — all under hand). Below each scene, a blank line for hidden count.

image_placeholders.description: Three Partner Hunt scenes in B&W line-art, each ~2in × 1.5in. Each shows a row of 5 snap-cubes with Penny's chef hand covering different amounts: Scene A 2 visible / 3 hidden, Scene B 4 visible / 1 hidden, Scene C all 5 hidden under the hand. The hand is drawn with a chef sleeve and apron edge visible.
image_placeholders.placement: Top half of the page, three scenes side by side.
image_placeholders.text_image_alignment_check: Image FORM_Q1_NUMBER_QUANTITY_MATCH: keywords (penny, hidden, cubes, showing) name what the scenes show.

prompts.answer_key: Scene A: 3 hidden. Scene B: 1 hidden. Scene C: 5 hidden. A child who gets all three correctly within 30 seconds shows recall (A6.11 mastery). A child who counts up to find each answer is emerging.

prompts.prompt: Look at the number line. Some numbers are missing. Fill them in.
prompts.visual_layout: A horizontal number line strip showing 0 to 20 with 4 cells empty. Numbers visible: 0, 1, 2, _, 4, 5, 6, 7, _, 9, 10, 11, 12, _, 14, 15, 16, _, 18, 19, 20. The empty cells (3, 8, 13, 17) have light dotted outlines for the child to write in.

image_placeholders.description: A horizontal number-line strip in B&W line-art spanning the full page width (~7in). 21 cells across (0-20), each ~0.6in × 0.6in. Cells 3, 8, 13, 17 have dotted outlines (empty, ready to fill). All other cells show their numerals in bold. A small Penny chef icon at the left end and Quincy piggy-bank at the right.
image_placeholders.placement: Middle of the page; full width.
image_placeholders.text_image_alignment_check: Image FORM_Q2_FILL_THE_NUMBER_LINE: keywords (number-line, missing, penny, quincy) name what the number line shows.

prompts.answer_key: 3, 8, 13, 17. A child who fills these in correctly shows count-on competence (A6.8). A child who restarts at 1 each time or skips numbers needs a re-loop on count-on before Lesson 4.

prompts.prompt: How are you feeling about partners of 5 and snack-shop stories? Circle the face.
prompts.visual_layout: Three faces in a horizontal row: a big smile, a neutral mouth, and a worried frown. Below each: 'GOT IT!', 'ALMOST!', 'TRY AGAIN!'. The child circles one.

image_placeholders.description: Three round face icons in a horizontal row, each ~1.5in across. Left face: smiling face with curved upturned mouth. Middle: neutral straight-line mouth. Right: downturned mouth. Below each, label: 'GOT IT!', 'ALMOST!', 'TRY AGAIN!'. Total row ~6in.
image_placeholders.text_image_alignment_check: Image FORM_Q3_FACES: keywords (got, almost, try) name the labels under the faces.

prompts.answer_key: Open. Compare with Prompts 1 and 2 results: confident self-rating + correct prompts = ready. Confident rating + wrong prompts = needs metacognitive bridge. Low rating + correct prompts = confidence-building.

formative_worksheets.teacher_notes: Administer this between Lesson 3 and Lesson 4. Print one per child; collect after 10 minutes. Score guide: 4/4 (3 partner-hunt + 1 number line) + confident self-rating = ready for Lesson 4. 3/4 = brief 1:1 conference. 2/4 or fewer = small-group re-loop on partners-of-5 OR count-on before Lesson 4. Children who get Prompt 1 wrong on the all-hidden scene (Scene C) often have a 'something must be visible' rule; the repair is to count all 5 together BEFORE the hide.

reflection_sheet.title: My Coin Counters Reflection
reflection_sheet.purpose: End-of-unit metacognition. Children look back at their week of money and operations work, rate themselves, name a favourite coin, name a struggle, and set a forward goal.
reflection_sheet.student_learning_goal: I can think about what I learned this week.

header.student_learning_goal_banner: I can think about what I learned this week.
header.character_watermark: Penny the Lead Counter holding a Junior Counting Crew certificate in the top-right corner. Small (~1.5in tall).

reflection_sheet.teacher_notes: Hand out at the very end of Lesson 5, after the summative worksheet. Allow children to take it home as a self-assessment artifact. Compare each child's reflection with their summative score: high reflection + high summative = ready for next unit; high reflection + low summative = bridge confidence; low reflection + high summative = celebrate and validate.
